chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the female performing Itikaaf, when she menstruates, he said: She should return to her house, and when she is clean, she returns, and she makes up for what is upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman's Itikaaf if she menstruates during the retreat?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the practical jurisprudence for female Itikaaf, distinguishing it from the male practice by mandating an exit to the home upon menstruation rather than remaining in the mosque. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that purity is a condition for the validity of the retreat's continuity, requiring the woman to resume her stay only after performing Ghusl and completing the missed days.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the female performing Itikaaf when she menstruates. Heasws said: ‘She should return to her house, and when she is clean, she would return, and she would make up for what is upon her’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a female in Ttikaf begins to experience Hayd (menses) she must go home; and after becoming clean return to complete Qada’ (compensatory ’Ttikaf) of what she owes.’”
